title: polyesternet
content:
it's almost the end of august and i haven't blogged all month! honestly, i haven't really felt much desire to, which i already kind of mentioned in my post last month. between heatwaves, my dad's dementia, and the general state of the world online and offline, i've been staying as disconnected from everything as much as possible and trying to find enjoyment in a more local and quiet existence. in my spare time, i've mostly been watching jdramas, listening to music, and sketching instead of doing things that require me to plug in and be connected to the larger world.

i did spend some time making my selections for the tiny awards. it was hard because there were so many good sites! in the end, i selected sites that required multiple visits to truly appreciate and to absorb so my picks leaned more towards denser ones rather than the kind that are more like single use/single purpose (but still interesting and amusing) web app type sites. i don't know if any of my picks made it onto the shortlist yet but it was a fun experience. the public voting phase opened today! go vote for your faves! a few of my picks made it into the shortlist so that made me happy ^-^

i haven't done much work on my homepage here in the past month. i've barely touched my computer at all (￢_￢;) i did add a few more friends to the links sections but that's about it. as i mentioned above, i'm kind of going through an existential time, especially with my online life. part of me thinks about retiring from the internet as it continues to deteriorate into more of a mess. unfortunately, looking at all the tiny award submissions didn't help much to restore good feelings about the current web. it was only a brief escape. in some ways it made me feel worse. because how are there are so many amazing things being done that hardly anyone sees or cares to see and that the primary use of the web is actually whatever torture device it has become? for every good site i visited last month, i probably saw five articles or videos about pervert glasses, flock cameras, the right-wing hate ecosystem, "ai" everything, gambling markets, data centers, etc, etc. i'm too tired of all this to link to specific examples but i'm sure if you've spent a few seconds online lately, you know what i'm talking about. i don't even seek out that stuff, it's just inescapably always in the periphery of being online. and it sucks to feel like this after i've spent pretty much my whole life telling people how amazing the internet is (could be.) it's polyester now, as the kids say these days.

given that this is the reality of the situation, i've just been questioning whether i need to write or publish anything online. i'm not looking for work or collabs or sponsorships or anything like that so do i really need to contribute to the overall internet content churn so diligently? i find myself just talking about how bad things are (this post is no exception) and fear becoming a broken record that doesn't really help make anything better. it is nice to meet new and interesting people through this page. but i still get emails regularly even if i haven't blogged in over a month. maybe i'll just stay on this "whenever i feel like it" homepage building and blogging schedule for now and write when i feel like i have something important to say (though this might mean i'll never write again if nothing feels important anymore (๑>ᴗ<๑)) but when things are too forced, it stops being fun.
